- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) in recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 2–5% to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.10), model often overpredicts; apply downward bias of 1–4% for the first 10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak or use exponential decay to smooth out.
- Model underestimates late in the 30-day horizon (last 7–10 days) when sentiment is weak; add 1–3% upward bias to compensate for mean reversion toward prior 18-day average.
- If sentiment history shows increasing positivity (e.g., 0.20 → 0.33 → 0.20), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 2–4% for the next 7 days to avoid overcorrection.
